en: Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering a total land area of approximately 109,965 square kilometers.
Standing at 2,954 meters above sea level, Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines.
The Main Crater Lake of Taal Volcano in Batangas sits at an elevation of just three meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching about 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of roughly 911 square kilometers.
The Philippine Trench, located east of the archipelago, reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters at the Galathea Depth.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon, making it the longest.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, spanning over 14,649 square kilometers including its islands.
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology monitors 24 active volcanoes across the archipelago, including the highly active Mayon Volcano.
The navigable underground river at Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan stretches for 8.2 kilometers.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters tall.
The Philippines has a coastline of approximately 36,289 kilometers, ranking fifth longest in the entire world.
